editorial:
Imagine a world where the biggest rock star in history is played by a woman. That is exactly what happens here. You get a wild, experimental look at John Lennon and Yoko Ono, but with an all-female cast. Instead of a boring history lesson, you get a playful movie that pokes fun at how famous couples argue and how they obsess over their own image. The vibe is very 80s, with the actresses dressed in mod clothes from the 60s. It feels less like a biography and more like a stylized piece of art that challenges how you think about fame.

What really works is the way it ignores the facts to tell a deeper truth. You will notice that the acting is more about the feeling of the era than being a perfect copy of the real people. Some parts might feel a bit slow or weird if you are expecting a traditional plot, but that is part of the charm. If you love indie films that break the rules, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that the real person behind the fame has vanished. Instead of a big dramatic finale, it focuses on the idea that John Lennon has become a symbol rather than a human being. The final scenes emphasize that we only see what we want to see in our idols. It ends by leaving you to realize that the celebrity image is just a mask we all agree to believe in.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird indie films and music history.
